description: Canonical descriptions of the ten generative deformation modes.

0.label: Silent Withdrawal
0.description: The geometry expands irregularly along its surface normals while subtle sinusoidal oscillations affect all three spatial axes.

1.label: Residual Relation
1.description: The geometry undergoes a noise-modulated rotational twist around its vertical axis.

2.label: Signal Interference
2.description: Rapid sinusoidal interference displaces the geometry along the horizontal and vertical axes.

3.label: Orbital Shear
3.description: The geometry is sheared through an orbital rotation in the XY plane while being displaced along the Z axis.

4.label: Matter Dispersion
4.description: A time-varying cellular wave pushes the geometry outward and inward along its surface normals.

5.label: Void Collapse
5.description: The geometry progressively implodes toward its center, with the collapse intensity modulated by procedural noise.

6.label: Fragment Vector
6.description: Selected high-noise regions are projected outward along radial vectors, producing shard-like fragmentation.

7.label: Spatial Distortion
7.description: The geometry is independently stretched and compressed along all three axes through time-varying anisotropic deformation.

8.label: Surface Flux
8.description: The surface flows laterally across the X and Z axes while undergoing a noise-modulated downward drift.

9.label: Entropic Drift
9.description: High-frequency oscillations affect all three axes while procedural noise introduces an additional chaotic spatial drift.
